title: Supplier economics & switch-cost lab: elasticity knobs, fallback ledger, and procurement heuristics
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Objective: produce an operationally-actionable report and small simulation harness that quantifies (1) model supplier price elasticity for common enterprise workloads, (2) the incremental latency+cost of fallback routes under capacity constraints, and (3) a switch-cost heuristic that procurement and Solutions Engineering can use when negotiating Dedicated/Private deals. The deliverable is a short report, a scoring ledger (CSV + dashboard) we call the 'fallback ledger', and a lightweight simulator that can run 3 prioritized enterprise scenarios. This differs from previous market scans by focusing on operational economics and switching friction (not just capability mapping).
acceptance_criteria: Simulator that runs three scenarios (embedding-heavy search, high-throughput chat, batch summarization) and produces per-scenario: latency distribution, per-token cost, fallback-route cost, and failure probability
Fallback ledger: CSV with scored supplier rows including metrics: nominal-price, latency-p50/p95, availability, fallback-cost, estimated-switch-cost, negotiation-sensitivity-index
Executive 6-page briefing with recommended procurement heuristics (two threshold policies) and a 1-page decision checklist for AE/SE
Dashboard tile in Console sandbox showing simulated cost/latency tradeoffs and ability to toggle elasticity knobs
Stakeholder review (GTM, Solutions Eng, Infra) signed off in comments before close

notes: Trade-offs discussed: depth of supplier telemetry vs time-to-deliver; decided to model coarse availability bands (99.5/99.9/99.99) rather than require per-vendor SLA ingestion for MVP.
We will surface both deterministic fallback costs (calculated from assumed per-token multipliers) and empirical fallback delta observed in trace replays.
This ticket intentionally avoids recommending vendor-specific procurement terms — we output heuristics and a scoring ledger for AE/SE to adapt per-deal.
